questions.topic: Tokenization Choices and Their Retrieval Consequences

questions.topic: Tokenization Choices and Their Retrieval Consequences
questions.question: A multilingual corpus uses one English punctuation regex. What is the likely failure?

questions.topic: Tokenization Choices and Their Retrieval Consequences
questions.question: Why does changing token boundaries normally require a full reindex?

questions.topic: When Stemming Helps Recall and Hurts Precision
questions.question: What is stemming?
options: Verification of exact phrases from stored token positions
Lookup of semantic synonyms in a curated dictionary
Heuristic reduction of word forms to a shared key
Removal of every high-frequency function word

questions.topic: When Stemming Helps Recall and Hurts Precision
questions.question: How can stemming improve recall?
options: By giving unrelated concepts separate exact identifiers
By keeping every surface-form distinction in its own posting
By dropping every query term that carries a suffix
By letting morphological variants share one lookup key

questions.topic: When Stemming Helps Recall and Hurts Precision
questions.question: A stem merges connection, connected, and connective. What failure may appear?

Every morphological variant becomes impossible to retrieve

questions.topic: When Stemming Helps Recall and Hurts Precision
questions.question: How does lemmatization differ from crude stemming?
options: It strips stop words from the text before tokenization
It maps inflected words to dictionary lemmas by linguistic analysis
It guarantees synonym matching across every supported language
It leaves irregular pairs such as mice and mouse unrelated

questions.topic: When Stemming Helps Recall and Hurts Precision
questions.question: What index design protects exact technical forms while still gaining stemming recall?

questions.topic: When Stemming Helps Recall and Hurts Precision
questions.question: Why do stemmed and unstemmed scores differ even for the same corpus?
options: Stemming leaves every dictionary and postings statistic intact
An unstemmed index drops term frequencies from its postings
Stemming changes only the capitalization of stored tokens
Merged variants change document frequency and rarity weight

questions.question: Why were stop words historically removed?
options: Their very frequent postings cost space and query work
They were the most discriminative terms for ranking
Removing them improved exact verification of phrases
They occurred in only one document per collection

questions.topic: Stop Words: Space Savings vs Phrase-Query Damage
questions.question: What capability is directly damaged when phrase terms are omitted from the index?

Exact phrase verification
Document-ID assignment

questions.question: Why is a generic English stop list risky for domain text?
